paragraphs: The X3 20d has been a mainstay of the X3 diesel range since 2012, spanning two generations under one badge. Early G01 models from 2012 to 2015 use the N47, a 2.0-litre diesel that's part of a family known for a specific timing chain issue. From late 2015 onwards, across both the G01 and later the G45, the X3 20d switched to the B47, a newer, significantly more reliable unit that doesn't share the N47's timing chain concerns. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and the known wear pattern differ - which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The X3 20d is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel fitted to the X3 20d xDrive from 2017 to 2024. This is a B-series generation engine, known for its improved reliability over earlier N47 units. We replace timing chains, bearings, and gaskets as standard on every rebuild.

A 3.0-litre six-cylinder diesel fitted to the X3 30d xDrive from 2017 to 2024. This is the larger sibling to the B47 and shares the same robust B-series architecture, generally considered reliable. We replace timing chains, bearings, and gaskets as standard on every rebuild.

A revised 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel fitted to the current X3 20d xDrive from 2024 onward. It's too new for any established wear pattern to exist, but we service it to the same high standard as the previous generation.

A revised 3.0-litre six-cylinder diesel fitted to the current X3 30d xDrive from 2024 onward. Like its four-cylinder counterpart, it's too new for a pattern to exist, but our specialist technicians are fully equipped to rebuild it.

compatibility.intro: Because BMW X3 20d can use the B47 or B57 engine code, fitting the wrong replacement risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:
